title: Region suitability & failover evaluation framework for enterprise residency requests
creator: Marina Velasquez
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers are increasingly asking for region availability guarantees and specific data residency (e.g., data must remain in EU or APAC), plus documented failover behavior. Current intake and prioritization are ad hoc: requests land in different channels, engineering effort is estimated inconsistently, and legal/regulatory checks are applied late.

Goal: Deliver a prescriptive evaluation framework that product, sales, and solutions engineering can use at first contact to: 1) decide feasibility, 2) score priority, 3) route to the right execution path (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), and 4) capture legal/compliance gating early. The framework should reduce friction, align cross-functional stakeholders, and produce a consistent SLA/failover proposal template for customers.
intake_form_template: Required fields for initial intake: customer name, account tier, requested region(s), residency constraints (data at rest, processing), desired failover regions and RTO/RPO expectations, anticipated request volume (RPS/peak/day tokens), compliance regimes (GDPR, SOC2, HIPAA, etc.), contract deadline, ownership (AE/CS/SE), legal contact, urgency rationale. Optional: architectural diagram, expected models, and latency targets.
triage_rubric: High-level triage steps: 1) Validate business fit (is request productized or custom?) 2) Determine routing: Hosted (if available region + low compliance needs), Dedicated (if throughput + isolation required), Private (if full residency or air-gap). 3) Legal gate: if residency implies data sovereignty or regulatory withholding, flag for legal review immediately. 4) Engineering feasibility: map to infra effort (new cloud region enablement, provisioning automation, storage replication). 5) Proposed timeline and cost estimate (one-time + recurring). Each step records a decision and owner in the ticket.
scoring_weights: Proposed priority scoring (0-10 each): strategic_impact: 40, regulatory_risk: 25, revenue_velocity: 15, implementation_complexity: -10 (higher complexity reduces score), customer_count_impacted: 10, SLA_need: 10. Thresholds: >=60 -> P0/P1 fast-track, 40-59 -> P1 Planned, <40 -> P2 backlog.
routing_matrix: If request == small customer + single region + standard compliance: route -> Hosted enablement + Account Exec standard doc. If request == high throughput + isolation: route -> Dedicated capacity TODO (cost estimate + reserved pool). If request == legal residency/air-gap: route -> Private deployment intake and legal/compliance workflow. If failover required across geopolitical boundaries, route -> cross-team architecture review + infra readiness assessment.
legal_and_compliance_checks: Early checks to perform: 1) Data classification (PII, health data, financial), 2) Residency vs transfer (is exporting data allowed?), 3) Contractual controls (data processing addendum, SCCs), 4) Local regulations (e.g., China, Russia restrictions), 5) KMS/HSM requirements. Outcome: 'Clear', 'Conditional (controls needed)', or 'Blocked'. Attach legal owner and expected turnaround.
failover_readiness_criteria: Minimum acceptance criteria for automated failover: identical model artifact availability in failover region, KV cache priming strategy, prefix cache fallback plan, latency SLA degradation profile documented, test-runbook for failover, playbook owner assigned. For manual failover: documented steps, expected RTO, and on-call rotation assigned.
acceptance_criteria: Framework published as single-page intake in Confluence and linked on SE playbook
Intake form added to internal CRM + automatic ticket creation in Linear
Legal gating checklist templated and legal owner assigned
Two example triaged requests completed to validate scoring and routing
